theGardenOfBones.title: Scenario IV-B: The Garden of Bones

intro.title: Scenario IV-B: The Garden of Bones
intro.part1:
The late autumn breeze howls through the Black Forest and into your bones when you step off the train. The air is thick with the scent of pine, and the overcast sky drapes a silvery pall over the towering steeple of Freiburg Minster. Your long journey to the city of Freiburg im Breisgau is at its end, but the hard part is yet to come.

When you passed through Berlin the locals welcomed you with open arms, eager to entertain American visitors—and to accept your American money. But Freiburg is different, and far less welcoming. The few locals walking the narrow cobblestone streets keep their heads down, as if they sense the trouble you've brought along with you. Right now, Freiburg feels less like a city and more like a trap, and each step you take away from the train station makes you feel like you're travelling further into a place that doesn’t want you there—as if the very wind is trying to push you out.
intro.part2: You've learned a lot since you picked up that first lead on Helena Nussbaum back in the Cavalier speakeasy. The elusive headmistress of Nussbaum Academy may have emigrated from Freiburg nearly fifty years ago, but your interactions with the locals reveal that her reputation here is still steeped in fear. They believed she was a witch, and as her wealth and influence grew, so did the suspicions about her true nature. By the time she left for America, Nussbaum and her followers had become the prime suspects in over twenty local murders and disappearances. Knowing what you know after wandering the dark halls of her school, it’s not hard to believe the stories might be true; in fact, you suspect she might be an aspect of one of the Three Mothers themselves. If she’s truly returned to her old stomping grounds, you suspect she plans to pick up right where she left off and resume terrorizing the city.
intro.part3: You've read through Frank Mandel’s file enough by now to know every word by heart. While stationed here during the great war, Mandel claimed to have seen visions of Mater Suspiriorum haunting the forest— visions that followed him all the way back to Arkham. After everything you've seen, you suspect that Mandel’s madness isn't the result of a mind broken by the horrors of war, but something even more terrifying. As you look out upon the thick forest on the horizon, the wind picks up, almost challenging you. If Mater Suspiriorum is out there in the woods, then you'll need to be ready to deal with the same terrors that the poor sergeant did. Hopefully, you'll make it through in better shape than he did—with your sanity intact.
intro.part4: You recall what you were able to learn from Dr. Armitage’s collection of books. Before Brother Ross returned to Wales and penned the essays that would later become the pages of Our Ladies of Sorrow, the monk spent a brief, unsettling period at Hirschau Abbey, a now-abandoned Benedictine monastery in the northern slopes of the Black Forest. Though he claimed to have uncovered the existence of her sisters only through later research, Ross insisted that the Mother of Sighs herself had at least one human aspect hidden deep in the Black Forest, secreted away in a convent dedicated to St. Walpurga. That detail stands out as the most concrete lead toward finding Mater Suspiriorum among the rest of the scattered clues in Armitage’s books. Driven by the slim hope that it might lead to something substantial, you're ready to trace the path Brother Ross left behind.
intro.part5:
It’s not just the wind that’s sending chills down your spine—it’s also the memory of Anna Kaslow’s voice, how it softened when she spoke of Mater Suspiriorum; not with fear, but with a trace of nostalgia, almost like she was recalling an old friend. “As a girl,” she recalled, “I did much more than tell fortunes. I was part of something much older—something woven into the fabric of the past, if you can believe it. Mater Suspiriorum wasn't a just a myth told to frighten naughty children— to me, she was my teacher, a guide through the dark corridors of our craft. A friend. When I knew her, she used the name Dorothea Spitznagel.”

‘She reflected the world’s sorrow, cared for those who suffered, took their pain into herself. And I? I looked to the world for hope—and hope blinded me to what she truly was.” Anna had smiled at you, then, the lines of age deepening around her eyes. “Go to Freiburg, in Germany,” she said. “Listen to the sighs on the wind, look with eyes that see beyond the obvious, and they'll lead you to her. But be warned: if you're not careful, she'll claim you and your pain, too.”
intro.part6:
Your heart feels heavy as you wander the cold streets of the city. Something's missing here—something vital, and the more you walk these twisting alleys, the clearer it becomes. Young people have been vanishing every night. You've managed to collect three leads— none of them good, but all pointing to one thing: Mater Suspiriorum, the Mother of Sighs.

Your first lead comes from a quiet, jittery shopkeeper in the Altstadt. He talks quickly, like he’s scared someone might hear. “Beneath the city,” he says, nodding toward the ground. “Old tunnels, catacombs—forgotten by most, but not by the witch. Some of those poor kids, the ones who vanished... they were down there, looking for her.”

Your second lead comes from a tight-lipped old woman, more interested in her knitting than whatever you had to say. “The Schauinsland,” she murmurs, not even bothering to glance up. “There's a tunnel carved through the mountain, for midwives traveling between Kappel and Hofsgrund in winter. People say, if you take the wrong path, it doesn’t just get you lost. It takes you to the other side of the world.”

The third clue finds you, not the other way around. A waif of a girl corners you in the shadows of the Münsterplatz. “My sister went into the Black Forest,” she says ominously, startling you as she appears from behind a corner. “She said she was going to find something... something that would take her sadness away. She never came back. They all say she ran off, or that she’s dead. But I know it’s not true. The witch took her.” Before you can question her further, she runs off into the crowd.

You're drawing closer to Mater Suspiriorum, but it’s not just about finding her anymore. It's about finding those kids, too. The people of Freiburg may be too frightened to do anything, but you're not.
intro.chooseLead: Choose one lead from your campaign log to follow.
intro.chooseStart: The investigators must decide where to begin the search.

effects.lead2: During setup, if you decided to begin the search in the city of Freiburg: Each investigator begins with 2 clues from the token bank.
effects.lead3: Before the first investigation phase, if you decided to begin the search in the Black Forest: Each investigator may choose to play an asset from their hand, paying its cost.

rules.title: Locations in The Garden of Bones
rules.body:
The locations the investigators will explore during act 1 and act 2 of The Garden of Bones are either single-sided with encounter card backs or double-sided with story card backs, and enter play revealed. For the best experience, do not look at the reverse side of these cards.

Locations in act 3 of this scenario are double-sided, and enter play with their unrevealed side up.

label.2: Follow the lead on Helena Nussbaum.
